11.11.44: and when I devour those fierce and great Vaiprachitta Asuras, my teeth shall become red like the flowers of the pomegranate.
11.11.45: Hence the gods in Svarga and men in the world of mortals, praising me, shall always talk of me as 'Red-toothed' (Raktadantika).
11.11.46: And again, after a period of a hundred years during which no rain and water shall fall, praised by the munis I shall be born, but not womb-begotten, on the earth.
11.11.47: Then, because I shall behold the munis with a hundred eyes, mankind shall therefore celebrate me as 'Hundred-eyed' (Shatakshi).
11.11.48: Next, O ye gods, I shall support the whole world with the life-sustaining vegetables, which shall grow out of my own body, during a period of heavy rain.
11.11.49: I shall gain fame on the earth then as Shakambhari; and in that very period I shall slay the great Asura named Durgama.
11.11.50: Thereby my name shall become celebrated as the goddess Durga. And again, when taking a terrible form on mount Himavat,
11.11.51: I shall destroy Rakshasas for the sake of delivering the munis; all the munis, bowing their bodies reverently, shall laud me then;
11.11.52: hence my name 'The terrible goddess' (Bhimadevi) shall become celebrated. When the Asura named Aruna shall work great trouble in the three worlds,
11.11.53: I shall take a bee-like form, the form of innumerable bees, and shall slay the great Asura for the welfare of the three worlds,
11.11.54: and folk shall then extol me everywhere as Bhramari. Thus, whenever trouble shall arise caused by the Danavas,
11.11.55: at each such time I shall become incarnate and accomplish the foes' destruction.

12.12.2: And whoever with mind composed shall praise me constantly with these hymns, I will quiet down every trouble for him assuredly.
12.12.3: And those who shall celebrate the destruction of Madhu and Kaitabha, the slaughter of the Asura Mahisha, and the slaying of Shumbha and Nishumbha likewise;
12.12.4: and those also who shall listen in faith to this poem of my sublime majesty on the eighth day of the lunar fortnight, on the fourteenth and on the ninth, with intent mind—
12.12.5: to them shall happen no wrong-doing whatever, nor calamities that arise from wrong-doing, nor poverty, nor indeed deprivation of their desires.
12.12.6: Never shall he experience fear from enemies, from robbers, nor from kings, nor from weapon or fire or water-flood.
12.12.7: Hence this poem of my majesty must be read by men of composed minds and listened to by them always with faith, for it is the supreme course of blessings.
12.12.8: Now may this poem of my majesty quell all kinds of calamities, which arise from grievous pestilence, and the three-fold portent.
12.12.9: Where this poem is duly read constantly at my sanctuary, I will never forsake that place, and there my presence is fixed.
12.12.10: At the offering of the bali, and during worship, in the ceremonies with fire, and at a great festival, all this story of my exploits must verily be proclaimed and listened to.
12.12.11: I will accept with kindliness both the bali worship that is paid, and the oblation by fire that is offered, by him who understands or him who understands not.
12.12.12: And at the great annual worship that is performed in autumn time, the man who listens filled with faith to this poem of my majesty
12.12.13: shall assuredly through my favour be delivered from every trouble, and be blessed with riches, grain and children.
12.12.14: From listening to this poem of my majesty moreover come splendid issues and prowess in battles, and a man becomes fearless.
12.12.15: When men listen to this poem of my majesty, enemies pass to destruction, and prosperity accrues, and their family rejoices.
12.12.16: Let a man listen to this poem of my majesty everywhere, at a ceremony for securing tranquillity, and after seeing an ill-dream, and when planets are greatly eclipsed.
12.12.17: Thereby portents turn into calm, and also dreadful eclipses of the planets, and also an ill-dream which men have seen; and a sweet dream appears.
12.12.18: It produces peacefulness in children who have been possessed by the demon that seizes children, and it is the best promoter of friendship among men when union is dissolved;
12.12.19: it is the most potent diminisher of the power of all men of ill livelihood; verily through reading it comes the destruction of Rakshasas, goblins and Pishachas.
12.12.20: All this poem of my majesty brings a man near unto me. And by means of cattle, flowers, arghya offerings and incenses, and by the finest perfumes and lamps,
12.12.21: by feasts given to brahmans, by oblations, by sprinkled water day and night, and by various other objects of enjoyment, by gifts yearly—
12.12.22: the favour which comes by such means, such favour is won from me when this story of my noble exploits is once heard. When heard, it takes away sins and confers perfect health.
12.12.23: This celebration of my births preserves created beings from evil spirits; and from this story of my exploits in battles, the annihilation of the wicked Daityas,
12.12.24: when it is heard, no fear that is caused by enmity springs up among men. And the hymns which ye have composed, and those composed by brahman rishis,
12.12.25: and those composed by Brahma, bestow a splendid mind. He who is surrounded by a raging fire in a forest or on a lonesome road,
12.12.26: or who is encompassed by robbers in a desolate spot, or who is captured by enemies, or who is prowled after by a lion or tiger or by wild elephants in a forest,
12.12.27: or who is under the command of an enraged king, or who is sentenced to death, or who has fallen into bonds, or who is whirled around by the wind, or who stands in a ship in the wide sea,
12.12.28: or who is in the most dreadful battle with weapons falling upon him, or who is afflicted with pain amidst all kinds of terrible troubles—
12.12.29: such a man, on calling to mind this story of my exploits, is delivered from his strait. Through my power lions and other dangerous beasts, robbers and enemies,
12.12.30: from a distance indeed, flee from him who calls to mind this story of my exploits.
12.12.32: Having spoken thus, the adorable Chandika, who is fierce in prowess,
12.12.33: vanished there, while the gods were gazing indeed on her. The gods also, relieved from fear, their foes being slain, all resumed their own dominions as before,
12.12.34: participating in their shares of sacrifices. And the Daityas—when Shumbha, that most fierce foe of the gods, had been slain by the goddess in fight,
12.12.35: he who brought ruin on the world and who was peerless in prowess, and when Nishumbha also, great in valour, was slain—the rest all came to Patala.
12.12.36: Thus that adorable goddess, although everlasting, yet taking birth again and again, accomplishes the safeguarding of the world, O king.
12.12.37: By her this universe is bewitched; she verily gives birth to the universe. And when besought, she bestows knowledge; when gratified, she bestows prosperity.
12.12.38: All this egg of Brahma, O king, is pervaded by her, who is Mahakali at Mahakala, and who has the nature of the great destroying goddess Mahamari.
12.12.39: She indeed is Mahamari at the fated time; she indeed is creation, the Unborn; she indeed, the Eternal, gives stability to created beings at their fated time.
12.12.40: She indeed is Lakshmi, bestowing prosperity on the houses of men while she abides with them; and she indeed, when she is absent, becomes the goddess of Ill Fortune unto their destruction.
12.12.41: When hymned and worshipped with flowers, and with incense, perfumes and other offerings, she bestows wealth and sons, and a mind brilliant in righteousness, and a happy course.

13.13.2: I have now related to thee, O king, this sublime poem, the Devi-mahatmya. Such majestic power has the goddess, by whom this world is upheld.
13.13.3: Moreover, knowledge is conferred by her who is the adorable Vishnu's Illusive power. By her thou and this vaishya and other men of discrimination
13.13.4: are bewitched, and celebrated men were bewitched; and others shall become bewitched. Go unto her, the supreme queen, as to a place of refuge, O great king.
13.13.5: She indeed, when propitiated by men, bestows enjoyment, Svarga and final emancipation from existence.
13.13.7: Having heard this his speech, king Suratha, that lord of men,
13.13.8: fell prostrate before the illustrious rishi who performed severe penances, and being downcast by his excessive regard for self and by the deprivation of his kingdom,
13.13.9: went forthwith to perform austerities; and the vaishya, O great muni, in order to get a vision of Amba, took up his station on a sand-bank in a river.
13.13.10: And the vaishya practised austerities, muttering the sublime hymn to the goddess. They both made an earthen image of the goddess on that sand-bank,
13.13.11: and paid worship to it with flowers, incense, fire and libations of water. Abstaining from food, restraining themselves, concentrating their minds on her, keeping their thoughts composed,
13.13.12: they both offered the bali offering also, sprinkled with blood drawn from their own limbs. When they continued with subdued souls to propitiate her thus for three years,
13.13.13: Chandika, who upholds the world, well-pleased, spoke in visible shape.
13.13.15: What thou dost solicit, O king, and thou, O rejoicer of thy family, receive ye all that from me; well-pleased I bestow it.
13.13.17: Then the king chose a kingdom that should not perish in another life, and in this life his own kingdom, wherein the power of his enemies should be destroyed by force.
13.13.18: Then the vaishya also, whose mind was downcast, chose knowledge—to be wise, knowing 'what is mine' and 'what I am'—knowledge that causes the downfall of worldly attachments.
13.13.20: O king, thou shalt obtain thine own kingdom in a very few days,
13.13.21: after slaying thine enemies; it shall be steadfast for thee there;
13.13.22: and when dead, thou shalt gain another birth from the god Vivasvat,
13.13.23: and shalt be a Manu on earth, by name Savarnika.
13.13.24: And, O excellent vaishya, the boon which thou hast besought of me,
13.13.25: I bestow it for thy full perfection; knowledge shall be thine.
13.13.27: Having thus given them both the boon that each desired,
13.13.28: the goddess vanished forthwith, while extolled by them both in faith. Having thus gained the boon from the goddess, Suratha, the noble kshatriya,
13.13.29: shall obtain a new birth through the Sun, and shall be the Manu Savarni.
